pairs.why: A's bowsprit and spars are thin like the real ship's, while B's bowsprit is a fat knob and its masts are more spindly and taller.
A's truss is a thin lattice like the real one, while B's is chunky with rounded tube ends; both lamp bodies are similar barrels with a U-bracket.
B's door is a tall, plain slab with thin hinges and two panels like the real door, while A adds a lantern, pot and bulky frame; both are arched where the real door is not.
A has the real duck's compact body with a short tail and a big head, while B stretches the body and sweeps the tail up.
A's wide, boxy head hood and side arm sit closer to the real head's horizontal barrel shape than B's rounded, shield-like head.
A's hull and masts are chunkier and simpler like the real ship, while B's masts and rigging are thin and tall.
A has thick, chunky posts and wide planks like the real card, while B has a narrow deck with thin rails and thin planks.
B's body is a slightly squarer block with tighter corners and thinner cords, while A is more pillow-like; the difference is small.
